The `source` array correctly references the project's own Git repository, which is expected for a `-git` package. There are no top-level commands or suspicious substitutions (such as `$(curl ...)`, `eval`, or `base64` decoding) that would be executed immediately upon sourcing the file.

Thus, running `makepkg --printsrcinfo` on this PKGBUILD is safe, as it will only parse metadata without triggering any potentially harmful operations.
</details>

The `build()` function runs a `pnpm` script that invokes `tauri build` with `--no-bundle` and `--offline`, ensuring no external network access or automatic bundling occurs. The build uses `--locked` and `--offline`, which restricts dependency resolution to previously fetched crates. All installation steps in `package()` involve copying pre-built binaries and static assets (icons, desktop file, license) into standard system directories, with appropriate permissions. There are no signs of obfuscated code, unexpected network requests, or system modifications outside the package directory. The operations are consistent with standard packaging workflows for a Tauri-based application.

No dangerous commands (e.g., `eval`, `curl|bash`, unauthorized downloads) are present. All tools used (cargo, pnpm, git) are declared in `makedepends`. The package disables LTO and debug info appropriately for release builds. There is no evidence of data exfiltration, remote code execution, or supply-chain tampering.
